correctness.rationale: The normal ring is B because y is integral and belongs to the common fraction field. For every exponent (a,b), the summand x^a y^b belongs to R exactly when its available mixed-generator capacity u(a) is at least the numerical-semigroup predecessor gap q(b). The condition for multiplication by every monomial of B is therefore u(a)>=Q(b). Missing monomials are enumerated using quotient/remainder mod each lambda_i and stars-and-bars, yielding the finite quotient length, while the n,n+1 semigroup blocks give the displayed binomial closed form. The companion stdlib script independently enumerates generator decompositions in 138 finite parameter cases; finite checks are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-dimensional normalization-defect colength and the complete ring-theoretic conductor are not supplied by the 2024 semigroup classification, nor by the 2021 study that gives two-sided delta estimates and a different double-point invariant. The proof computes monomial membership via a capacity criterion, then counts the missing normal monomials; the logical steps are not merely a restatement of prior dimension bounds. A 2018 surface-specific predecessor could contain overlapping special cases and was not completely accessible, so historical priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The exact finite normalization colength is a natural map-germ and nonnormality invariant studied by the same authors; their earlier same-object work gives only estimates. The conductor ideal further quantifies gluing of the smooth normalization to the singular ring. A uniform all-dimensional exact formula, a computable conductor for arbitrary coprime exponents, and a closed binomial law for the natural consecutive-generator family are useful for singularity comparisons and provide more information than finite determinacy or an isolated known numerical table.
